title: Depth under duality and coordinate restrictions
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, and assign to each coordinate one of three states: free, fixed to $1$, or fixed to $-1$. For each binary input, form a sign vector by encoding each free bit as $1$ or $-1$ and using the assigned signs at fixed coordinates; restrict $f$ by evaluating it on this vector. If the dual function is $f^*(x)=-f(-x)$, then for every assignment of coordinate states, the restricted dual has the same minimum decision tree depth as the restriction of $f$ obtained by interchanging the two fixed states and leaving free states unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: An arbitrary state assignment for every coordinate, each free or fixed to $1$ or $-1$
